$comment: Maps runtime dependencies to their codebase context for /app:runtime-upgrade. One entry per runtime SDK: where the integration lives, what confines it, where changelogs come from, which SDK exports we touch, and package-specific upgrade judgment (upgrade_notes).

upgrade_notes: SDK 0.2.113+ ships a native binary and no longer bundles cli.js: CLI path resolution (sdk-utils.ts) and onboarding assumptions are version-sensitive; verify resolveClaudeCliPath behavior on any bump crossing that line.

The pin lives in SEVEN places and they must all move in one commit: root package.json pnpm.overrides (the only one that actually binds while an override exists), apps/server, apps/desktop and packages/cli dependencies, the two apps/desktop optionalDependencies (-darwin-arm64, -win32-x64), and CLAUDE_SDK_VERSION in services/runtimes/claude-code/tooling/provision.ts. scripts/__tests__/dependabot-lockstep-families.test.ts guards the manifest half; provision.ts's own test guards the seventh.

Never cite a line number in sdk.d.ts. It grew 7429 -> 8978 lines in the 0.3.224 -> 0.3.268 range alone, and every line citation in the codebase pointed at unrelated text afterwards. Cite the symbol (SDKUserMessage.shouldQuery), and in the minified bundle cite the string literal, never the symbol.

An in-session tool's input schema must contain no z.record() and no z.json() at any depth. SDK 0.3.257+ converts tool schemas through the installed zod's own processor with a context it builds itself, and zod 4.5.3+ record handling (zod #6497) dereferences a `deferred` field that context lacks: one offending schema throws inside tools/list and the model is handed ZERO DorkOS tools, silently. UPSTREAM: anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript#454, still OPEN as of 2026-09-22 with three reporters, and reproduced locally at 0.3.280 with zod 4.6.5 (z.record and z.json both still throw inside tools/list; the catchall form lists the tool). The root cause is the bundled zod-to-json-schema@3.25.2, which is already the latest published version, so no converter bump upstream can fix it (2026-09-21 upstream comment). The workaround is the z.object({}).catchall(...) swap documented in mcp-tools/tool-exposure.ts, across four schemas. ON THE NEXT BUMP: check whether #454 is fixed, and if it is, revert the catchall swap back to z.record()/z.json() — it is a workaround, not a preference, and it costs the JSON Schema its propertyNames bounds plus two measured value-level differences (see connector-schemas.ts).

result.modelUsage and total_cost_usd are RUNNING TOTALS, never one turn's figures: cumulative across warm turns in streaming-input sessions (observed live at 0.3.268 too), and since 0.3.277 carried across a resume or fork when the transcript saved them. sdk/turn-usage.ts differences each result against a per-session ledger for the per-turn gen_ai.* figures; re-check the modelUsage / total_cost_usd docblocks on every bump for a change in lifecycle (a /clear reset, a new carry-over rule).

The model catalog lives in the platform BINARY, not in sdk.mjs or sdk.d.ts, and DorkOS lists models by ALIAS (supportedModels() in messaging/runtime-cache.ts), so a bump can silently move `opus` / `default` to a different model and price (0.3.280: `opus` -> claude-opus-5-5). Read the new binary's alias table on every bump and name any retarget in the changelog. Moving CLAUDE_SDK_VERSION is what invalidates the on-disk model cache.

canUseTool and the tool hooks carry MCP server provenance since 0.3.274 (`mcpServer` / `mcp_server`: { name, source }). Trust keys on source === 'sdk' via isHostServedOrUnattributed in mcp-tools/tool-exposure.ts, never on the mcp__dorkos__ prefix alone; absent provenance must keep passing for non-MCP tools and older CLIs.

sdk_surface_map.$comment: 27 distinct symbols across 45 non-test files, re-derived by parsing every `import … from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk'` on the 0.3.280 bump (2026-09-22; the 0.3.268 figure of 55 files was not reproducible). Paths are relative to codebase_root.

non_import_couplings: sessions/project-slug.ts hand-mirrors the SDK's session-slug hash algorithm (incl. the 200-char cap) with no import — grep/ESLint/surface-map all miss it; re-diff the sdk.mjs hash body on every bump, by STRING not by minified symbol (every symbol it has ever cited was renamed by the next release). Unchanged at 0.3.280 (byte-identical body, 200-char cap).

messaging/plugin-activation.ts hand-mirrors the Options plugin shape without importing it. The two DIVERGED at 0.3.268: SdkPluginConfig gained an optional skipMcpDiscovery the mirror deliberately does not carry. Still assignable, so nothing breaks — but re-read both shapes on every bump. Unchanged at 0.3.280.

sdk/sdk-utils.ts resolveClaudeCliPath() resolves the SDK's platform optional-dep packages by name (no SDK import); version-sensitive since the 0.2.113 native-binary split. Eight published variants at 0.3.280, unchanged, and none of them -android.

services/mesh/mcp-revocation.ts (outside the adapter dir) reasons about SDK-internal MCP connect timing with a fixture-pinned test that passes even when stale — re-observe on every bump. Re-derived statically AND re-run live at 0.3.268 (second fixture committed beside the first). At 0.3.280 the McpServerStatus status union is unchanged (it gained additive source? and tools[]._meta?), but 0.3.274 made the first turn STOP waiting for settings-file and plugin MCP servers whose tools tool search defers, so such a server can again read `pending` in the first system/init frame (tunable with CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_MS). `pending` is not evidence, so a revoked server may be caught one turn later; the live re-run of the two-server 401 harness at 0.3.280 is recorded in research/runtime-upgrades/claude-agent-sdk/0.3.268-to-0.3.280/triage-decisions.md.

sdk/sdk-error-mapping.ts reasons about the CLI's own abort predicate — its cause collapse and its suppression set — read out of the shipped binary and quoted in research/20260903_claude-cli-aborted-refusal-shapes.md, which carries the recipe. No import, no grep hit, no failing test. Re-run at 0.3.268: the suppression set GREW to three members and a new `turn-abort` cause collapses into `interrupt`. Re-run at 0.3.280: it grew again, to FOUR — interrupt, turn-abort, refusal-fallback-edit, permission-stop (raised when a deny decision ends the turn, mapped to turn_teardown). No DorkOS impact by construction: isStoppedTurnResult ANDs the shape with DorkOS's own stop record.

upgrade_notes: Versions track the Codex CLI release train and an active `alpha` dist-tag exists alongside `latest`; a fix may ship in alpha weeks before stable (the 0.143.0 logs_2.sqlite fix did). Check dist-tags when resolving the target, and never pin an alpha without an explicit user decision.

Follow the pinned-SDK bump checklist in contributing/adding-a-runtime.md (section: Bumping a pinned SDK): dist-tag check, .d.ts diff of the ThreadEvent/ThreadItem unions and imported item types, event-mapper exhaustiveness compile, runtime conformance suite, one live smoke turn.
The event mapper's `never` exhaustiveness checks fail compilation when the SDK adds union members; that is the intended upgrade tripwire, not an obstacle to suppress.

The CLI pin is version-coupled beyond the SDK's type surface, and sdk_surface_map cannot see it: model-catalog.ts speaks the app-server `initialize` + paginated `model/list` protocol by hand, and model-context-windows.ts parses the CLI's own models_cache.json and rejects it whenever its `client_version` differs from the running binary (so every CLI bump blanks context-window enrichment for one 300-second freshness window). Neither file imports the SDK, so no .d.ts diff can ever flag them — verify the model picker live after every bump.

changelog_sources.note: Authoritative version list, publish timestamps (.time), and the latest/alpha dist-tags
Release tags are prefixed `rust-v` (e.g. rust-v0.142.5): strip the prefix when matching npm versions. Releases cover the whole Codex CLI, not just the SDK; filter notes for SDK/TypeScript relevance.

upgrade_notes: The SDK is only the HTTP client. The `opencode serve` sidecar binary ships as a SEPARATE package (`opencode-ai`, resolved via runtimes.opencode.binaryPath or PATH) and version-couples with the client: assess every SDK bump against the sidecar versions users actually run, and state the supported binary range in the upgrade spec.
npm dist-tags include dozens of `0.0.0-snapshot-*` channels; `latest` is the only meaningful channel: never resolve a target from any other tag.
Server-driven contract: most behavior lives in the sidecar, so release notes about the server can matter more than client-visible API changes even when no imported type changed.

Some adapter code matches upstream ERROR TEXT rather than a type: the subagent mapper decides stopped-vs-failed from the `task` tool's error string. No type diff can catch a change there, and 1.18.20 made one (a new `Subagent failed (task_id: ...): ...` envelope around a cancelled child). On every bump, diff the upstream task tool, session runner and processor at the target tag for the strings they emit on abort, interrupt, cancel and failure.
